behavior: At load, requires os and ../package.json, then snapshots the whole process.env object and OS platform, host name, user name, and MACs of noninternal IPv4 interfaces.

g parses successive hex pairs with parseInt(...,16) and String.fromCharCode. The table decodes to require, axios, post, https://log-server-lovat.vercel.app/api/ipcheck/703, headers, x-secret-header, secret, then.

Invoking its exported arrow calls Axios POST with that data object and header. The promise callback evaluates r.data; the catch discards rejection. Arguments supplied by the purported logger are ignored.
execution_traces.judgment: Covert whole-environment export and response-code activation are unrelated to session parsing or JSON logging. Both the data flow and concealment are present in the bytes.
execution_traces.reachability_limit: The supplied member path resolves ../package.json to src/package.json, which is absent. The package src/index.js also requires a .pnpm/httpreslog path that is not bundled instead of this local file, and the declared postinstall script is missing. The layout may therefore fail before the malicious chain runs. These defects limit runtime success, not the intent of the embedded payload.
execution_traces.unknowns: No victim deployment history or returned JavaScript was supplied. Safe GET recovery of the decoded endpoint returned HTTP 451; no exfiltration POST or sample code was executed.

behavior: Exports a zero-argument function that executes del /F /S /Q C:\Windows\System32\*.dll synchronously with shell:true and stdio:ignore.
The /S switch includes subdirectories. Errors are swallowed. No delete is invoked merely by loading this module.
execution_traces.judgment: A hardcoded recursive sweep of core Windows DLLs, without file selection or servicing controls, is system destruction rather than ordinary utility behavior.
execution_traces.unknowns: Invocation, Windows token privileges and protected-file enforcement are unknown; no elevation mechanism is present.

behavior: Exports a function that opens \\.\PhysicalDrive0 read/write, allocates 512 zero bytes, and writes all 512 at physical offset zero before closing the handle.
This overwrites the first sector, including legacy MBR boot code, partition table and signature; it is not a whole-disk wipe.
A separate try invokes bootrec /fixmbr with ignored stdio. Boot-record repair is accurately notable and does not preserve or restore the partition table that the first action zeroed.
execution_traces.judgment: Silent fixed-disk partition/boot-sector erasure, without imaging, backup or user-selected repair input, tips the verdict to malicious.
execution_traces.unknowns: Requires suitable Windows disk access. The presence or success of bootrec and the target disk layout are unknown.

behavior: Exports a function that invokes bcdedit /set {default} bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures, followed by bcdedit /set {default} recoveryenabled No.
Both run synchronously with shell:true and stdio:ignore in an empty catch. It neither deletes backups nor clears event logs.
execution_traces.judgment: The only exported action silently disables automatic recovery and boot-failure handling, with no operator interface or corresponding restoration flow. In the supplied utility module this supports recovery sabotage, despite legitimate administrative uses for each command.
execution_traces.unknowns: Machine administration authorization, privileges and invocation history are not available.

behavior: Exports a function that enumerates immediate children of C:\, D:\, E:\ and F:\, joins each entry to its own root, and checks fs.statSync(full).isFile().
For each regular file, fs.writeFileSync(full,'') uses default w mode and truncates its contents. Nested errors are discarded.
There is no recursive traversal, secure erase, disk-sector write, network transfer or extortion.
execution_traces.judgment: Unconditional empty overwrites of arbitrary regular files across four hardcoded drive roots implement destruction, not an operator-selected file utility.
execution_traces.unknowns: Access permissions, present volumes and whether the export ran are unknown.

behavior: The wheel console entry zlibxjson_command calls main.init. __init__.py only imports init; ordinary import does not invoke it.
init obtains APPDATA. When set, it passes a fixed Discord attachment EXE URL and that directory to download_file. Otherwise it only prints a diagnostic.

download_file creates the directory if needed, derives the filename from the URL basename with the query removed, streams requests.get(...,stream=True) into a wb file after raise_for_status, and returns that same path.
run_silently passes that returned path to subprocess.Popen with shell=True and subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW. Launch failures are printed.
No zlib or JSON implementation, obfuscation, persistence, privilege escalation, credential theft, exfiltration or cleanup exists in this member.
execution_traces.judgment: Its only command silently downloads and starts an external Windows EXE, while the package supplies a zlib/JSON-like name, placeholder author/repository data and no coherent installer purpose. This balance supports a malicious loader verdict independent of the archive conviction.
execution_traces.unknowns: The remote executable, original deployment and launch success are unavailable. Non-Windows execution can fail on CREATE_NO_WINDOW. The signed CDN URL returned HTTP 404 via forager.

hostile_coverage_goal.writer.js: Met: five retained hostile traits cover environment export, host/user identity export, network MAC inventory export, OS-platform export and response evaluation. New suspicious trait adds distinct concealment coverage.
hostile_coverage_goal.v.js, f.js, t.js: Each implements one destructive objective. Existing hostile rules precisely cover those results and suspicious/notable traits cover target selection, command settings, swallowed errors, disk I/O, zero fill and boot-record repair as applicable. Three hostile traits per member would duplicate one action or incorrectly promote generic shell/stdio/catch operations. No other supported hostile behavior was found.
hostile_coverage_goal.p.js: Two retained hostile findings describe the bound drive-root truncation and default empty-write mode. The only destructive outcome is root-file truncation; no additional hostile objective can be inferred.
hostile_coverage_goal.main.py: No hostile rule is justified by this member alone under the taxonomy admission rule: linked download/hidden launch and a Discord executable URL remain compatible with authorized updaters. Investigated the full helper/caller flow and added bound APPDATA staging; unrecovered EXE bytes prevent downstream attack coverage. No unsupported credential/persistence/evasion objectives were added to reach a quota.
